title: openai-compat: map OpenAI function/tool schemas + tool_choice semantics + streaming tool message formatting
author: Aarti Shah
release_notes: Enhances OpenAI compatibility: maps OpenAI function/tool JSON Schemas to Redwood tool descriptors, implements tool_choice semantics (explicit selection + fallback), and stabilizes streaming formatting for tool messages. No API-breaking changes to Redwood's existing endpoints; opt-in via 'openai_compat: true' in model config.
description: This PR improves Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling. Motivation: many downstream customers expect 1:1 semantics with OpenAI-style tool schemas and the tool_choice behavior they rely on. We add two pieces: (1) a schema mapping layer that converts OpenAI 'functions' JSON Schema into Redwood tool argument descriptors (flattening nested 'properties', preserving required/optional semantics, mapped types, and examples), and (2) explicit tool_choice semantics similar to OpenAI: model responses can indicate tool_choice with a tool name and optional arguments; Redwood will attempt exact-name match, then fuzzy match, then fall back to a configurable default-tool route. Additionally, this PR tightens streaming output for tool messages: tool-invocation events are emitted as boundary-delimited JSON chunks (event: "tool_call", payload: {tool, args}) and tool output is streamed in 'tool_output' events with stable chunk framing so SDKs can reassemble reliably. The description below covers motivation, design, and compatibility notes. Implementation details: - openai_compat/mapper: new module to translate OpenAI function schemas into redwood/tool descriptors (preserves types, enums, descriptions, and examples; creates top-level param names for nested objects using dot-notation by default). - openai_compat/choice: adds deterministic matching logic for tool_choice and exposes fallback policies (first-match, default-tool, reject). - runtime/streaming: small streaming framing additions to emit 'tool_call' and 'tool_output' event types and include sequence ids; ensures server-side buffering flushes at API boundary to avoid partial JSON tokens for clients. - sdk-python and sdk-typescript: updated README and client-side streaming parsers to recognize new event types; added helpers to reconstruct nested args from dot-notation. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in behind 'openai_compat' flag in model config and does not change existing Redwood tool invocation paths. Known limitations: nested schemas with polymorphic types (oneOf/anyOf) are flattened into a string union and surfaced as 'one_of' validation on the Redwood side; planned follow-up PR will add richer oneOf resolution and typed coercion. See linked Linear tickets ENG-2142 (schema mapping) and ENG-2165 (streaming stability + tool_choice).

Ran compatibility checks against an existing customer prompt corpus.
changelog_text: OpenAI compatibility: improved function/tool schema mapping and tool_choice semantics; stabilized streaming events for tool calls and outputs. Opt-in via model config 'openai_compat: true'.
example_request: POST /v1/chat/completions (openai-compat) with functions=[{name:'get_weather',parameters:{type:'object',properties:{location:{type:'string'}}}}] results in a tool_call event: {event:"tool_call",payload:{tool:'get_weather',args:{location:'seattle'}}} followed by tool_output events containing the tool stdout in chunks.
follow_up: ENG-2204 planned: richer oneOf handling and schema coercion; ENG-2199 planned: add automatic alias registration to reduce fuzzy matches for common tools.
